messages:
maya: FYI escalating a GDPR deletion request from AcmeHealth (org_id: acme-987). They want: full deletion of user data (user_email: jane.doe@acmehealth.com), confirmation that backups and any KMS/HSM-wrapped secrets are handled, and an audit-proof export showing removal. Customer is urgent, legal looped in.

olivia: Thanks Maya — can you paste the DPA/DSR ticket details and whether they signed the standard DPA? I can prep comms if we get the technical proof.

sam: Quick asks from security: 1) Is the data only in application layer payloads or also in structured logs? 2) Which KMS keys are in use (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)? 3) Where is the tenant pinned region? We need repro steps + request IDs to verify deletion traces.

maya: Ticket: DSR-2025-047. DPA is standard signed DPA v2. Customer region: eu-west-1 (confirmed). Initial report: they called our API to purge user objects but want assurance that HSM-backed keys / snapshots aren't keeping retrievable copies.

maya: Repro steps I tried (from support shell):
```bash
# attempt delete via Admin API
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/orgs/acme-987/users/purge \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SUPPORT_TOKEN}" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"email":"jane.doe@acmehealth.com","reason":"gdpr-dsr"}' -v
```
Response: 202 Accepted
Response body: {"job_id":"job-11a2b","status":"pending"}
Logs show backend request_id=rxA1bC3.

maya: Follow-up: polled job status
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.run/v1/jobs/job-11a2b -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SUPPORT_TOKEN}"
```
Status: finished, deleted_objects: 42, deletes_from_s3: true

sam: Good — include the raw request_id/trace IDs and any database tx IDs. We will check whether any log indexing pipeline retained the payload. If logs retained, we need to redact and re-run retention purge.

raj: KMS/HSM note: For this tenant we use Redwood-managed KMS keys in eu-west-1 with CloudHSM-backed keys (key alias: rw/acme-987). Important: if we delete ciphertext blobs from S3/DB, but retain the KMS key, the key itself doesn't contain plaintext. If the key is customer-managed (CMK), the customer controls key lifecycle. If they ask us to rotate-and-delete, we can schedule key rotation or key disablement; full cryptographic destruction requires key material deletion which we can only do for Redwood-managed keys. For CMK we can provide instructions to customer-managed KMS.

lena: From Legal: we need to provide a signed confirmation of deletion (DPA clause). Suggested proof: (a) job_id & timestamps, (b) storage object list + confirmation they were wiped, (c) audit log export showing no access after deletion, (d) KMS key status and action taken. Can Security provide a short statement we can attach?

sam: I will pull audit log slices for request_id=rxA1bC3 and job-11a2b. Preliminary: index shows the delete job executed at 2025-03-10T14:22:03Z, user payload removed from primary DB and S3 prefix s3://redwood-eu/acme-987/users/jane.doe@acmehealth.com. I see three log entries in clickhouse ingestion that contain masked email; need to check whether payload was fully in logs or only metadata. If payload present, we'll add a retention purge for those indices.

maya: Customer asked specifically about backups and snapshots — do we have a standard backup retention and purge process for eu-west-1 region? They want assurance their PII isn't in backups.

raj: Backups: nightly DB snapshots stored for 30 days in encrypted form (encryption key: rw/backup-eu). For customer data removal within backup window we follow the DSR flow: mark records for redaction, trigger snapshot rewrite for affected partitions, and update audit. That can take up to 72 hours for full rewrite for older snapshots. Note: if they want key destruction for old backups, we must confirm whether backup key is Redwood-managed. It's currently managed by Redwood.

olivia: Can we give a timeline to the customer? They asked for confirmation by EOD tomorrow. Is that feasible?

sam: Timeline: I can produce the audit export + log purge plan within 24 hours. Raj estimates backup rewrite up to 72 hours. Legal will need the deletion confirmation template signed; Lena, can you confirm if a self-signed Security statement is acceptable or if Legal needs to sign?

lena: Legal will sign the confirmation once Security provides the factual statement (what was deleted, timestamps, method). We prefer a standard footer and a PDF. Provide specifics and I'll attach the DPA clause reference.

maya: Proposed customer message draft (please edit):
"We processed your data deletion request (job-11a2b) on 2025-03-10T14:22:03Z. Affected objects were removed from primary storage and the delete job completed. We are processing backup rewrite for older snapshots (estimated completion within 72 hours). Audit exports and a signed deletion certificate will follow within 24 hours. KMS keys are Redwood-managed for this tenant; we will rotate and schedule key material destruction for backup keys once rewrite completes."

sam: Edits: change "schedule key material destruction" to "schedule key material destruction where permitted under operational safeguards" — we need Operations & Legal to sign off on exact phrasing. Also add a reference to the audit export ID (audit-export-20250310-acme987).

raj: I'll run a DB query to confirm the primary rows are gone and attach the query result (tx_id: dbtx-77f). ETA 2 hours.

maya: Thanks all — I'll send the draft to the customer after Legal + Security sign-off. Assigning action items: Sam -> audit export + log purge plan (24h); Raj -> DB + backup rewrite status (72h); Lena -> sign-off template; Olivia -> customer comms.

audit-bot: [+deleted_objects=42] job-11a2b completed by support.maya at 2025-03-10T14:22:03Z (trace=rxA1bC3).

maya: I'll update thread once Raj and Sam confirm. :thumbsup:
